# Energy Efficiency KPI Testing and Reporting

This procedure is used to measure Energy Efficiency for selected Energy Saving States - by default: `OnAirBefore`, `ESM1`, `ESM2`, `OnAirAfter`. Each measurement (for a single state) takes 75 minutes.

- Energy Efficiency KPI is calculated and reported based on [report_esm_kpi](https://wrgitlab.ext.net.nokia.com/RAN/resource-packages/taf.rfrl.common_resources/-/tree/master/taf/rfrl/common_resources/ee_kpi?ref_type=heads).
- KPI results are stored in [KPI ReP](https://rep-portal.ext.net.nokia.com/reports/kpi/?category=EE_KPI&limit=25&test_run__end_db=30) for further analysis and comparison.

## About the Procedure

### Energy Saving States Mapping to Real Scenarios

- **OnAirBefore / OnAirAfter**
  - All `PSGRP` and `NRPGRP` in `suspended` state.
  - All RUs reconfigured to `NORMAL` `energySavingMode`.
  - Unblock all GSM and WCDMA cells (if any).
  - All cells on air.
- **ESM1**
  - Enable configuration with regard to the `ESM1` configuration defined in the YAML file.
    - Waiting until cells are in the expected state (YAML-defined cells).
    - Waiting until RUs are in the expected state (YAML-defined RUs).
- **ESM2**
  - Enable configuration with regard to the `ESM2` configuration defined in the YAML file.
    - Waiting until cells are in the expected state (YAML-defined cells).
    - Waiting until RUs are in the expected state (YAML-defined RUs).

### High-Level Test Steps

0. **Requirements**
   - Ensure `actPowerMeter`, `actNrLBPowerSaving`, `actLBPowerSaving` are enabled and `mtBtsEnergyMonitoring`, `mtSBTSRfmEnergyMonitoring`, `mtSBTSSmEnergyMonitoring`, `mtSBTSBBCAPEnergyMonitoring` are set to 15-minute intervals.
   - Configure `PSGRP` and/or `NRPGRP` on the BTS according to your requirements (see details under [Configuring Energy Saving – Summary](#configuring-energy-saving--summary)).
   - Param `actRadioDeepSleepTimeSchedule` should be set to `false`
   - Prepare `esm_configuration.yaml` file according to your test scenario. See [Sample ESM Configuration file](#sample-esm-configuration-file) for details.
1. Go to the `OnAirBefore` state and wait for all cells to be `OnAir`.
2. Get EE counters before measurement.
3. Check if Cells and RUs status is stable during the 75-minute measurement (check every 30 seconds). Counters are calculated from 4 PM periods (the first one is ignored).
4. Get EE counters after measurement.
5. Calculate and report ESM KPIs for `OnAirBefore`.
6. Repeat steps 1–5 for the remaining test states: `ESM1`, `ESM2`, `OnAirAfter`.
7. Restore the initial configuration using delta recommissioning.

### `Run ESM Measurement Procedure` Keyword Parameters

- `connection`: Admin CLI connection alias.
- `configuration_yaml_file`: Path to the ESM configuration YAML file(absolute or relative).
- `test_states`: Test states separated by commas. Default: `OnAirBefore,ESM1,ESM2,OnAirAfter`.
- `measurement_duration`: Duration of the test in seconds. Default: 75 minutes per loop.

## Sample Test Case and Execution

In most cases, you only need to provide the `connection` parameter to the keyword. Other parameters are optional and have default values or will be generated automatically.

```robot
*** Settings ***
Resource    taf/rfrl/procedures/SISO/ESM/resources/ESM.robot

*** Test Cases ***
Sample ETSI Test Case
    # Remember to connect to ADMIN CLI and then pass the connection to the keyword
    Run ESM Measurement Procedure
    ...    connection=connection_alias
    ...    configuration_yaml_file=esm_configuration.yaml
```

### Remarks

> **Note**  
> KPI results are not reported immediately. They will be parsed by the **ute_reporting_portal** script and added to the Robot report.

> **Note**  
> If you run the test suite manually, please remember to use the **ute_reporting_portal** command after execution finishes.

> **Note**  
> Please use the `Run ESM Measurement Procedure` keyword only once in a single test case. If you want to run this procedure with a different configuration, do it in separate test cases. This is important for proper result interpretation in PowerBI.

## How is it Visible in ReP?

- Data is visible in the JSON file:

```json
"kpi_results": [
    {
        "id": "00035",
        "value": "2024.00",
        "source": "EEKPI",
        "variant": {
            "smod": ["ASIB", "ASIM"],
            "rmod": ["AQQF"],
            "rat": ["5G"],
            "object": "RMOD-31",
            "energy_state": {
                "cell": {
                    "NRCELL-313": {
                        "energy_saving_state": "energySaving"
                    }
                },
                "rmod": {
                    "RMOD-31": {
                        "power_state": "SLEEP"
                    }
                }
            },
            "serial_number": "K9234728707",
            "bbmod": ["ABIP"]
        },
        "entity_id": "MRBTS-81058"
    }
    ...
]
```

- Each KPI is reported in a new format (similar to OAM KPIs):

    ```python
    {
      'id': <kpi_id>,             # KPI id from KPI source definitions (filled automatically based on KPI name)
      'value': <value>,           # Calculated by Report ESM KPI
      'variant': <variant of KPI> # Generated automatically by Report ESM KPI KW
      'target':  <target>,        # Optional
      'source': 'EEKPI'           # Source of KPI definitions (for report_oam_kpi KW it's always OAMKPI)
    }
    ```

- Data is also visible in the main view of the test run,
- And can be found in the KPI table at: https://rep-portal.ext.net.nokia.com/reports/kpi/

  During reporting, **KPI Name** and **KPI Description** are not provided directly—they are automatically gathered from the source KPI definition (maintained by Verification Architects).  
  For more information about the KPI report table, see [ReP documentation](https://confluence.ext.net.nokia.com/display/LRP/KPI+Report).

## Configuring Energy Saving – Summary

Energy saving states for cells are managed using `PSGRP` (LTE) and `NRPGRP` (5G) groups. You can create multiple `PSGRP/NRPGRP` groups and assign cells to them as needed for testing. The configuration can use default values, but pay attention to the following parameters:

- `lbpsCellSOOrder`: Higher value means the cell will enter `energySavingState` later within the group.
- `lbpsLastCellSOEnabled`: Must be set to `true` for the last cell in the group to enter `energySavingState`. If there is only one cell in the group, this must also be `true`.
- `lbpsSuspended`: Controls whether the rule is suspended. If suspended, cells will not enter `energySavingState`.
- `lbpsSOMethod`: By default, the whole cell is switched off. You can also configure to switch off only the TX.
- `lbpsMonWinForCellSOff`: Default is 300 seconds. Lowering this value will make cells enter `energySavingState` faster.

### Shortest test duration

Historically, it was assumed that only one cell per PSGRP/NRPGRP group would enter `energySavingState` at the same time, and that multiple cells in a group would enter it one after another, each after the `lbpsMonWinForCellSOff` period (default 5 minutes). In practice, you can define several cells in one power group and have them all enter `energySavingState` at the same time. For that to work, set for each cell in the group `lbpsCellSOOrder=100` and ensure `lbpsLastCellSOEnabled=true`. If you use different `lbpsCellSOOrder` values or omit these settings, cells in the group will still enter `energySavingState` sequentially, and the time to reach it will be longer.

To reduce the time to `energySavingState` further, you can additionally set the following in `/rom/swconfig.txt`:

```
#LowLoadSwitchOffDelay, 0x110016 (range: 0~60, default: 30; Defines number of 10s periods of low load)
0x110016=3
0x5900AA=3
```

## Configuring DeepSleep – Summary

- To allow a Radio Unit (RU) to enter `SLEEP` state, all carriers must be switched off. This means all cells assigned to the RU must be either in `energySavingState` or blocked.
- When no cell is active under an RU, the radio will enter `SLEEP` state after about 5 minutes. 
  - Not all radios support `SLEEP` state; this depends on the RMOD type. If the `powerState` is `UNAVAILABLE`, the radio does not support DeepSleep.
- To configure DeepSleep, change the `energySavingMode` parameter from `NORMAL` to `DEEPSLEEP` for the selected RMOD.
  - By default, the RMOD will enter `SLEEP` state as soon as possible. If `actRadioDeepSleepTimeSchedule` is enabled, you can define specific hours when the RMOD is allowed to enter `SLEEP` state.

## Sample ESM Configuration File

```yaml
CONFIGURATION:
    ESM1:
        LNCEL-1:
            lbpsSOMethod: Cell Switch Off
        LNCEL-2:
            lbpsSOMethod: Tx Switch Off
        NRCELL-1:
            lbpsSOMethod: cell switch off
        NRCELL-2:
            lbpsSOMethod: TX switch off
        RMOD-1:
            energySavingMode: DEEPSLEEP
        RMOD-2:
            energySavingMode: DEEPSLEEP_EXTREME_SFP
        BLOCK_WCDMA_GSM_CELLS: False
    ESM2:
        NRCELL-2:
            lbpsSOMethod: cell switch Off
        RMOD-2:
            energySavingMode: DEEPSLEEP
        BLOCK_WCDMA_GSM_CELLS: True
```
- `lbpsSOMethod` possible values (Note the difference in capitalization for NRCELL and LNCEL cells):
  - LNCEL
    - `Cell Switch Off`
    - `Tx Switch Off`
  - NRCELL
    - `cell switch off`
    - `TX switch off`
- `energySavingMode`
  - `DEEPSLEEP`
  - `DEEPSLEEP_EXTREME_SFP`
- `BLOCK_WCDMA_GSM_CELLS`: true/false
